newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SENEGAL TO PUSH TAIWAN'S CASE FOR ENTRY TO WHO.
newsitem.headline: SENEGAL TO PUSH TAIWAN'S CASE FOR ENTRY TO WHO.

text.p: Senegal has proposed putting Taiwan's quest for observer status in the World Health Organisation (WHO) on the formal agenda of the agency's annual Assembly starting next week, the WHO's chief said on Friday.
Director-General Hiroshi Nakajima told a news conference he had passed the African state's request to the general committee of the Assembly, which opens on May 5.

The committee is composed of a rotating total of 25 of WHO's 191 member states. It was not yet clear whether China -- which could be expected to oppose Taiwan's bid -- would be among the members this year.

However, even if the committee does not approve the request as a special agenda item, the Assembly may still debate the issue and pass a resolution requesting Nakajima to issue an invitation to Taiwan to observe the forum, officials said.
"It is the Assembly which decides," Nakajima said.
The Assembly is being held from May 5-14 to decide the 1998-99 budget and set policy guidelines.

Nakajima last month rejected Taiwan's request for observer status as no such category exists at the Geneva-based agency, although a member state may propose inviting a country or entity to observer the annual forum.
The (South) African National Congress (ANC) and Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO) received observer status to attend the annual talks in 1974.

Taiwan's Foreign Minister John Chang said on April 23 that his country had decided to take part in the WHO because it was the least politically sensitive body of all U.N. organisations. He called on Beijing not to block its bid.

China has regarded Taiwan as a rebel province ineligible for international recognition since a civil war split them in 1949, and has blocked its membership as a sovereign state in all international forums since 1971 when the General Assembly assigned the Chinese U.N. seat to Beijing.
